summary: Jessie Pons is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. She completed her doctoral thesis at Paris-Sorbonne University in 2011 and served as Junior Professor in South Asian History of Religion at Ruhr University Bochum (attested 2019).
Ji Hao is a sinologist who earned his PhD at the University of Minnesota under doctoral supervisor Paul Rouzer. He held a post at the College of the Holy Cross (attested 2017).

Ji Zhe specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and sinology. After earning a Ph.D. in sociology from the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences in 2007, he served as Associate Professor at INALCO (attested 2011–2017).
Jian Deng is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a disciple under Weijue Shi, whom he later succeeded in 2005.

Jian Ouyang was a Buddhist studies scholar and philosopher who studied under Yang Wenhui from circa 1904 to 1911. He founded the China Inner Studies College, serving as its head from circa 1922 to 1943.

Jiang Wu specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology, having studied at Nankai University and Harvard University under Tu Weiming, Robert M. Gimello, Peter K. Bol, and Zhichao Chen. He served as Professor at the University of Arizona (attested 2011–2018).
Jianming Hu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (attested 2015). In 2015, he held a researcher position at Komazawa University.
Jiaqi Wang was a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology who studied under Gangkar Rinpoche and was a PhD student at Columbia University (attested 2026).

Jiayao An is a historian, archaeologist, and sinologist who studied under Bai Su from circa 1979 to 1982. Beginning around 1982, she held posts as a special researcher and Xi'an research office director at the Institute of Archaeology, CASS.

Jiegang Gu was a sinologist and historian-archaeologist who studied at Peking University (~1913–1920) under Taiyan Zhang and Hu Shih. He held posts at Peking University, Fudan University, the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.
Jien Abe was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who was a graduate student at the University of Tokyo (attested 1973). He served as a professor at Meiji University until 2001.

Jifu Lan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who studied at Tunghai University (~1965–1969). He served as a full-time researcher at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies from circa 1985 until his retirement in 2019.

Jigdal Dagchen Sakya was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Ngawang Thutop Wangchuk, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche. He held a post at the University of Washington from circa 1960 to 1963.

Jigme Chhoeda is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied at Tango Monastery and Druk Sangag Choeling Monastery under several traditional teachers. He served as Abbot of Tango Monastery and held Lopen posts in the Central Monastic Body and Dratshang Lhentshog.
Jigme Chökyi Sengge is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.
Jigme Tenpai Nyima studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Patrul Rinpoche, and Terton Sogyal, and taught Terton Sogyal and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Jigmeth Junu is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MA at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Yongdong Shi and traditional teacher Hui Xian (attested 2013).
Jikai Fujiyoshi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post at Kyoto University (attested 1967) and served as a professor at Rissho University.

Jikidō Takasaki was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned PhDs from Savitribai Phule Pune University and the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at the University of Tokyo and Waseda University, and was President of Tsurumi Women's University.

Jim G. Shaffer is an archaeologist and Indologist who earned his B.A. at Arizona State University and his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin–Madison. He served as a professor of anthropology at Case Western Reserve University from circa 1976 to 2012.
